correctness.rationale: Exact edge-split identity proves PD(A)=k plus internal splits crossed. An inductive delete-leaf/suppress-vertex argument proves exhaustiveness of all unrooted binary shapes generated by subdividing each edge. Recursive center canonicalization resolves unlabelled tree isomorphism. The standalone Python program exhaustively evaluates integer cross moments for all shapes n<=13 and all nontrivial k up to complement symmetry, with strictly positive minima; at n=14,k=6 it checks all 135 shapes and detects exactly one negative topology. Independently computed caterpillar moments N=3003, SX=47619,SY=55627,SXY=882033 give covariance -122/7007 and are reproduced by graph-pruning. These checks are finite and exact, not evidence about untested n.

value.rationale: The observable is the covariance of two complementary conserved evolutionary subtree lengths when species are partitioned without replacement, a natural phylogenetic complementarity question. Exhaustive positivity through thirteen leaves and a first negative fourteen-leaf caterpillar with exact rational covariance establish a sharp structural boundary, including uniqueness for the six-versus-eight split. This is not a new name for a standard marginal variance; it distinguishes joint from marginal rarefaction information. Its scope is appropriately finite, and it does not purport to quantify sampling noise or arbitrary branch lengths.
